newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Ed shuts Fermi 2 nuke for refueling.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Ed shuts Fermi 2 nuke for refueling.

text.p: Detroit Edison Co said Friday it began shutting the Fermi 2 nuclear power unit in Newport, Mich., a scheduled 52-day refueling and maintenance program.
The unit was operating at 50 percent of capacity late Thursday, and expected to be off line in cold shutdown late today or early Saturday, company spokesman Lew Layton said.
In addition to replacing spent fuel rods, the utility will replace three low pressure turbines and perform other plant improvements, he said.
Fermi 2 had been producing at below its 1,116 megawatt capacity since it returned to operation on Jan 18, 1995.
The unit was out of service for more than a year after one of the turbines threw a blade, causing extensive damage to the facility in December 1993.
Fermi 2 accounts for 11 percent of Detroit Edison's installed generation capacity and up to 16 percent of its daily electricity output.
Detroit Edison, a subsidiary of DTE Energy Co, is the operator and sole owner of the Fermi 2 unit. The utility serves more than two million customers in southeastern Michigan.
